 Comment React Share Moïse Kouame Reaches Brest Quarterfinals After Gaston's Unexpected Retirement
 Two years after winning his first professional match in Brest, Moïse Kouame reaches the tournament's quarterfinals. A qualification earned in unusual circumstances against Hugo Gaston.
 Moïse Kouame during his first-round loss to fellow Frenchman Ugo Humbert at the 2026 Monte-Carlo Masters 1000. © JEAN CATUFFE / DPPI VIA AFP Jules Hypolite 29/10/2026, 19:07 1 min to read Follow us Brest Gaston Kouame Moïse Kouame has advanced to the quarterfinals of the Brest Challenger.
 The 17-year-old Frenchman, ranked No. 176 this week, benefited from the retirement of top seed Hugo Gaston. Gaston threw in the towel early in the second set, with Kouame leading 7-5, 2-1.
 Remove ads A retirement with unclear reasons
 The reasons behind Gaston's retirement remain unknown, as no apparent physical issue seemed to be bothering him.
 Kouame continues his run in Finistère, two years after announcing himself at this very tournament by winning his first-ever professional match at just 15 years old.
 He will now face Francesco Maestrelli, ranked No. 174, with a spot in the semifinals on the line.
 Notably, the young Frenchman is also expected this weekend at the Paris Masters 1000, where he is set to compete in qualifying — unless he goes all the way in Brest.
